name: Congreve Hall
use: Residence hall, 272 students, all class years

renovations.what: Steam-fired domestic hot-water heaters (end of useful life) put out to bid for replacement with one heater in Congreve serving Congreve, McLaughlin and Lord

facts.text: Designed by Professor Eric T. Huddleston and built in 1920 as the second women's dormitory on campus.
Built with money borrowed from the Alice Hamilton Smith Fund and repaid from residents' rents; named for her first husband, Charles McIlvaine Congreve.
Houses 272 students of all class years, with five community lounges and a gender-inclusive community bathroom on each floor.
One of the few UNH halls with air conditioning and an elevator; it also has roll-in access and a roll-in shower.

verdict: Huddleston's 1920s Georgian Revival dorm facing the T-Hall lawn, with A/C, an elevator and lounges students call hotel-like.
notes: Old row's room mix (113 singles etc.) and 'undated modernization' were not confirmed on the current hall page, which lists amenities but no room counts; when A/C and the elevator were added is not documented. The 2024 hot-water work is confirmed only as a bid notice; completion not confirmed. Style left null: photos show a multi-wing brick building with slate roofs, dormers, a tall arched central window and a circular forecourt lawn (reads as Colonial/Georgian Revival), but no source names the style. Reference aerial (UNH Housing) shows a symmetrical U-shaped composition facing an oval lawn; interior not photographed in what I downloaded. Licensed photo (2007): seen across the T-Hall lawn, the long brick front with a gabled central pavilion, tall arched multi-pane window and slate roof with dormers reads as a dignified Georgian/Colonial Revival composition.
judgeNotes: Photo and aerial show a well-proportioned brick complex with a glazed gable over the courtyard. Exterior down a point from the old run: handsome, not a landmark.
